decisions.title: Non-compliant and unrecognized members
decisions.issue: JSON:API forbids additional members in defined objects while requiring implementations to ignore non-compliant members.
interpretations: Reject every unknown member.
Ignore non-compliant members while validating recognized content.
decisions.peer_behavior: No maintained peer fixture is pinned; the normative format controls this behavior.
decisions.selected_behavior: Core and Atomic decoders ignore unrecognized members while continuing to validate recognized content.
decisions.rationale: Ignoring non-compliant members preserves forward compatibility without weakening recognized-member validation.
decisions.security_consequences: Ignored members cannot satisfy required structure or activate application semantics.
decisions.resource_consequences: Unknown-member scanning remains subject to configured byte, depth, member, and value limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: New unknown members do not break otherwise valid documents.
decisions.wire_consequences: Ignored members are not emitted when the document is marshaled again.
decisions.upstream_status: The requirement is present in the JSON:API 1.1 format; no erratum is required.
decisions.reconsider_when: A later JSON:API version changes unknown-member handling.

decisions.title: Extension namespaces and profile authority
decisions.section: Extensions, Extension Members, Profiles, and Content Negotiation
decisions.issue: JSON:API defines extension and profile authority but does not prescribe a safe runtime registration mechanism.
interpretations: Activate semantics from every declared URI.
Require explicit immutable registration before activating semantics.
decisions.peer_behavior: No maintained peer matrix is pinned across all member scopes.
decisions.selected_behavior: Extension members and profile validators become semantic only through explicit immutable registration.
decisions.rationale: Registration prevents untrusted declarations from activating code or weakening core validation.
decisions.security_consequences: Untrusted extension and profile declarations cannot activate callbacks implicitly.
decisions.resource_consequences: Registered callback execution remains bounded by codec and document limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Unknown profiles remain declarations and unknown extension members follow JSONAPI-DEC-001.
decisions.wire_consequences: Registered members round-trip only at their declared object scope.
decisions.upstream_status: Official extension and profile registries remain the upstream authorities.
decisions.reconsider_when: JSON:API defines a safe discovery and activation mechanism.

decisions.title: Query parameter families
decisions.issue: JSON:API reserves query families but leaves filter, pagination, and implementation-specific semantics application-owned.
interpretations: Preserve every query parameter.
Accept only core and explicitly registered implementation or extension families.
decisions.peer_behavior: No maintained router peer is pinned because routing and backend execution are outside this package.
decisions.selected_behavior: Parse core families and accept implementation or extension families only through explicit registration.
decisions.rationale: Explicit registration keeps generic parsing separate from application query semantics.
decisions.security_consequences: Unknown families cannot silently activate backend behavior.
decisions.resource_consequences: Parameter count, name, value, and nesting limits bound parser work.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Registered custom operators remain explicit and local to the configured parser.
decisions.wire_consequences: Ordering and explicit empty values are preserved; malformed or unknown families return structured errors.
decisions.upstream_status: JSON:API 1.1 defines no standard filter operator vocabulary.
decisions.reconsider_when: A base revision or applied extension standardizes an application-owned family.

decisions.title: Relationship objects and linkage
decisions.issue: Relationship objects may contain several qualifying members while linkage has absent, null, to-one, and to-many forms.
interpretations: Require data in every relationship.
Accept any qualifying member and preserve the exact linkage form.
decisions.peer_behavior: No maintained peer fixture is pinned across every request and response context.
decisions.selected_behavior: Require one qualifying recognized member and preserve absent, null, to-one, and to-many linkage distinctly.
decisions.rationale: The selected behavior follows the relationship object contract without inventing authorization or persistence semantics.
decisions.security_consequences: Ignored members cannot satisfy required relationship content or authorize mutation.
decisions.resource_consequences: Relationship validation remains bounded by document limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Applications retain responsibility for authorization and persistence.
decisions.wire_consequences: Absent, null, to-one, empty to-many, and nonempty to-many linkage remain distinct.
decisions.upstream_status: No known erratum changes the relationship minimum-member rule.
decisions.reconsider_when: JSON:API changes relationship membership or contextual linkage rules.

decisions.title: Included-resource uniqueness and full linkage
decisions.issue: Included resources must be unique and fully linked while identity may use id or lid aliases.
interpretations: Compare only type and server id.
Build one alias-aware identity graph and apply the sparse-fieldset exception.
decisions.peer_behavior: No maintained peer graph implementation is pinned; specification-derived fixtures are retained.
decisions.selected_behavior: Use an alias-aware identity graph, reject duplicate resources, and require full linkage except for the exact sparse-fieldset exception.
decisions.rationale: One identity graph prevents alternate aliases from bypassing uniqueness and linkage checks.
decisions.security_consequences: Alias-aware uniqueness prevents identity confusion and duplicate-resource substitution.
decisions.resource_consequences: Graph traversal remains bounded by document resource and relationship limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: The sparse-fieldset exception applies only when the relevant relationship field was excluded.
decisions.wire_consequences: A resource cannot appear twice through alternate id and lid aliases.
decisions.upstream_status: No known erratum changes id and lid aliasing for compound documents.
decisions.reconsider_when: A future revision changes local identity or full-linkage semantics.

decisions.title: Sparse fieldsets
decisions.issue: JSON:API standardizes fieldset syntax but not application schema, authorization, or projection behavior.
interpretations: Project generic maps inside the package.
Parse fieldsets and leave schema-aware projection to applications.
decisions.peer_behavior: Framework peers combine parsing and serialization, but no equivalent transport-neutral peer is pinned.
decisions.selected_behavior: Parse ordered fields and preserve explicit empty presence while leaving schema validation, authorization, and projection to applications.
decisions.rationale: Generic parsing cannot safely infer an application resource schema.
decisions.security_consequences: The package never projects or authorizes unknown application fields.
decisions.resource_consequences: Fieldset parsing remains bounded by query limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Applications may apply their own typed schema and authorization policy.
decisions.wire_consequences: Ordered field names and explicit empty fieldsets are preserved.
decisions.upstream_status: JSON:API defines no application schema registry.
decisions.reconsider_when: A typed schema integration supplies an authorization-safe projection contract.

decisions.title: Pagination parameters and links
decisions.section: Query Parameters, Links, and Page Meta
decisions.issue: Base JSON:API leaves pagination strategy open while the optional Cursor profile defines concrete behavior.
interpretations: Apply cursor rules to every page family.
Activate cursor rules only through the profile API.
decisions.peer_behavior: No maintained peer fixture is pinned; the published profile examples are retained as authority evidence.
decisions.selected_behavior: Preserve generic page parameters and activate Cursor profile parameters, links, metadata, and errors only through the profile API.
decisions.rationale: Optional profile behavior must not become an implicit base JSON:API requirement.
decisions.security_consequences: Cursor values remain opaque and applications retain responsibility for integrity and authorization.
decisions.resource_consequences: Page size and cursor parsing are bounded by profile and query limits.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Base users may retain non-cursor pagination strategies.
decisions.wire_consequences: The canonical profile URI remains `http://jsonapi.org/profiles/ethanresnick/cursor-pagination/` while its monitored document is retrieved over HTTPS.
decisions.upstream_status: The Cursor Pagination profile remains a separately published optional profile.
decisions.reconsider_when: JSON:API standardizes base pagination or the profile publishes an incompatible revision.

decisions.title: Atomic operation order and rollback
decisions.issue: Atomic Operations requires ordered all-or-nothing processing but does not define a reusable Go transaction lifecycle.
interpretations: Validate document shape without execution support.
Require a caller-supplied transaction lifecycle with bounded failure handling.
decisions.peer_behavior: No maintained cross-language transaction executor fixture is pinned.
decisions.selected_behavior: Validate before beginning, apply operations in order, validate results before commit, and attempt rollback exactly once after a post-begin failure.
decisions.rationale: An explicit transaction adapter preserves extension ordering while leaving datastore isolation application-owned.
decisions.security_consequences: Validation precedes side effects and callback panics become bounded typed errors.
decisions.resource_consequences: Callbacks execute sequentially and cancellation stops further operations.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Applications retain responsibility for durable isolation and commit-unknown handling.
decisions.wire_consequences: Results preserve operation order and partial success is never emitted as a valid response.
decisions.upstream_status: Atomic Operations remains an official extension rather than base format text.
decisions.reconsider_when: The extension changes processing order, result correspondence, or atomicity.

decisions.title: Recommendation status
decisions.issue: JSON:API recommendations describe conventions that are not base conformance requirements.
interpretations: Enforce recommendations as protocol validation.
Document recommendations without making them package wire requirements.
decisions.peer_behavior: Frameworks enforce local conventions, but those conventions are not portable conformance evidence.
decisions.selected_behavior: Document useful recommendations without rejecting a base-compliant document for recommendation differences.
decisions.rationale: Informative guidance cannot be promoted into normative validation silently.
decisions.security_consequences: Recommendation-only behavior cannot activate routing, filtering, or method override implicitly.
decisions.resource_consequences: Applications remain responsible for bounding any convention-specific backend work.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Applications may add stricter local conventions without changing package conformance.
decisions.wire_consequences: Base-compliant documents are accepted regardless of recommendation-only naming or URL conventions.
public_apis: Documentation and examples; no recommendation-only validator
decisions.upstream_status: The recommendations page remains separate from the normative format.
decisions.reconsider_when: A recommendation is promoted into normative base, extension, or profile text.

decisions.title: Conflicts between authorities
decisions.issue: Base, extension, profile, recommendation, example, and application text have different authority and may conflict.
interpretations: Let the most specific artifact override base behavior.
Apply each artifact only within its declared authority and block unresolved contradictions.
decisions.peer_behavior: Peer popularity does not determine normative authority.
decisions.selected_behavior: Apply base rules first, constrain extensions and profiles to their authority, treat recommendations as informative, and block unresolved direct contradictions.
decisions.rationale: Separating authorities prevents lower-strength guidance from weakening base conformance.
decisions.security_consequences: Lower-authority artifacts cannot disable base validation or resource limits.
decisions.resource_consequences: Authority checks add no unbounded runtime work.
decisions.compatibility_consequences: Moving behavior between authority classes requires compatibility review.
decisions.wire_consequences: Base, extension, profile, recommendation, and application behavior remain separately labeled.
public_apis: All parsing, validation, negotiation, extension, and profile APIs
decisions.upstream_status: No unresolved direct contradiction is recorded at this revision.
decisions.reconsider_when: A governing authority publishes a conflicting erratum or revision.
